chapter: Leaving Duke and the Goodman sextet
title: The Ellington band after Cootie and Johnny left
summary: They discuss the 1940 band, the last session Concerto for Cootie, Ben Webster and who left next.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, -- well, let's just see about that. Now, just a second. One minute. Because you went with Benny for one -- I'll go back to that, because I want you to tell me about that very much. But the thing is, in 1940 -- so -- I wonder when Ben went with the band. Was Ben with the band? Yes.
Yeah, Ben must have been.
Yeah. Ben Webster must have been with the band when you were there.
Yes.
So -- well, all right, let's see. You went out of the band.
Yeah.
Rex was already in the band.
Yeah.
There was you, Rex and some first trumpet player.
Wallace Jones.
Yeah. Wallace Jones. So when you went out, he got Ray?
Yeah. Ray took my place.

He got Ray. Well, that's funny. I don't -- I didn't take down any more of those titles after I got to 1940, because I knew that's what we wanted to talk about then. Well, I tell you what though, I remember, because that was just coming up before the war.
But the time I'm speaking of, Helen, --
When?
When he had Louis Bellson and what's the alto player's name?
Willie Smith?
Willie Smith.
Oh, Yeah.
In the band.
Oh, yeah.
That period of time when he was recording. He made some recordings.
Yeah.
The band sounded wonderful.
Yeah.
It was a different sounding band.
Yes, it was a different sounding band, that's true. Because Louie made a very different sound in the band, too.
Yeah.
Cootie, incidentally, on that subject, did -- did -- had Sonny -- did Sonny leave after you two left, or -- I can't remember what happened there. Do you? Sonny was still with the band when you left.
Yeah. Everybody was there.
Yeah. You left.
When I left.
Then Johnny left not too long after, was it?
No. Was it Johnny? I done forgot it.
Yeah. But I mean, I never did know -- did Sonny just -- or did Sonny fall sick or something?
Maybe Sonny was taken sick or something.
Yeah. And was Sonny replaced by Louis Bellson, or was he replaced by somebody else?
I don't know. I was gone.

I don't remember. Yeah. But -- but the sessions I remember -- well, the band, you know, reached many peaks, but one of the peaks was right then, just before you left, when they made "Perdido", "KoKo", and those things that Ben Webster contributed a tremendous amount to. In the band. Remember around that time?
Yeah.
When you were there?
Yeah, I was there.
You were there. I guess -- well, as a matter of fact, I guess it was the last session you made before you left. I believe.
Yeah, the last session -- no. The last session I made was "Concerto for Cootie". I remember that.
Yeah. Yeah. That's what we said, in 1940. As a matter of fact, I don't think Ben remained for a very much longer time after that, I don't believe.
I don't recall.
No.
Who was the next one to leave after that.
No.
I think it was Barney Bigard?
Oh, yes. Oh, yeah. Was Barney still in the band when you left?
Yeah.
Oh. Yeah, I guess that was Barney, then. Well, you know -- well, one thing, you see, the band stayed almost intact for like ten years. And then, when you went, you know --
